profile.title: Profile and settings
profile.intro: Client details and the advisor's judgment for the case. Every case is different: none of this comes from the country.
profile.birthDateHint: Sets the age at the cutoff date.
profile.sexHint: Used by the default retirement age.
profile.dependentsHint: Children or other people who depend on them financially.
profile.typeHint: Sets the rules that apply in the plan.

types.rentista: Lives on rental or investment income

rules.empleado: Bonus (prima): split it among annual pockets, debts and savings by priority. Severance (cesantías): it is savings for housing or education, not emergency fund liquidity.
rules.contratista: Review months without a contract and each month's social security; a pocket for months without income. With no employee benefits, their own savings replace them. Confirm the contribution base, because it sets the pension.
rules.independiente_variable: The budget is built on the base income: the lower of the 12-month average and the average of the 3 lowest months. Anything above that is split with a fixed rule.
rules.pensionado: The net pension is the main income and health is already deducted. Check whether they still work; focus on liquidity and succession.
rules.rentista: Rental income is the main income: review months without a tenant and who pays building fees and property tax.
rules.mixto: The rules of each type of income they have apply.

help.emergencyMonths: How many months of essential spending the emergency fund covers in the worst scenario, if income is lost. More months are suggested the less stable the income is. The goal never goes below one month of essentials and, while there is expensive debt, it stays at that month.
help.expensiveDebtThreshold: From this rate up, a debt is considered expensive. While there is expensive debt nothing is invested, because no investment reliably earns more than that debt costs: the surplus goes to pay it off first.
help.pctInvestConfirmed: Share of each month's surplus that goes to investment when the reality check confirms that actual savings reach at least 85 % of the expected amount. The rest stays as margin.
help.pctInvestPending: Share of the surplus that goes to investment while the reality check is pending or shows unrecorded expenses. It is smaller because that surplus has not shown up in the account yet.
help.pctSurplusToDebt: With expensive debt nothing is invested: this share of each month's surplus goes to pay it off. It also applies to today's money left over after filling the fund, the months without income and the pockets.
help.pctExcessToInvest: Without expensive debt, the share of today's money that goes to investment as a one-off contribution: what is left of the liquid balance after keeping the cushion and filling the fund, the months without income and the pockets. With expensive debt, the debt percentage is used.
help.cushion: Money left in the everyday account and not allocated. The rest of the liquid balance goes to the fund, the months without income, the pockets and, if anything is left, the excess.
help.retirementAge: Age at which the client expects to stop working. In the 10 years before, the % in growth goes down gradually; with less than 5 years to retirement, the risk capacity goes down.
help.realReturnGrowth: Annual return above inflation assumed for money in growth in the projection. It is illustrative and not guaranteed.
help.realReturnStability: Annual return above inflation assumed for money in stability in the projection. It is illustrative and not guaranteed.
help.glideStep: Points the % in growth goes down each year in the 10 years before retirement, to reach that age with less risk.
help.growthFloor: The % in growth does not go below this floor, unless today's is already lower.

covers.vehiculo: Vehicle damage and theft. Confirm who pays it today.

hints.executive_summary: Three to five lines: the situation in one sentence, the three priority actions and the expected result.

hints.today: The main indicators and brief context.
hints.attention: Points of attention with the reason why, without alarm.
hints.action_plan: Balance allocation and pockets, contributions, debts if applicable, investment (profile, range by age and allocation) and protection (insurance and succession).
hints.calendar: Next 30 days, 90 days and 12 months, and key dates (end of debts, goals).
hints.tracking: Tracking indicators with their target value.
hints.scope: It is based on the information provided; figures are estimates in today's values; no product recommendations; taxes, pension and legal matters with the corresponding professional.
hints.closing: A positive summary, pending items and the next review.
hints.body: Write one paragraph per idea; a line that starts with “- ” is a bullet.

It does not include recommendations of financial products or institutions. You should confirm tax, pension and legal matters with an accountant, your pension fund and a lawyer.
